title: HSC Youth Ambassador Program

description: The Hamburg Sustainability Conference (HSC) Youth Ambassador Program 2027 is inviting young community leaders from Global South countries to become part of an international cohort working to advance solutions to sustainability challenges. benefits: The call offers a fixed professional fee for the development of the dossiers.
howToApply: Applications must be submitted in English through the official online application form. Applications submitted through other channels, as well as incomplete or late applications, will not be considered.
The application form requires candidates to explain their motivation and experience, propose topics for their selected sector or sectors and submit a short writing fragment.
Applicants should prepare their materials carefully because the selection process assesses both professional suitability and the quality of their proposed content.
Yes. The call states that there are no geographical limits. Applicants from outside Europe may apply if they meet the requirements.

The SALTO Participation and Information Resource Centre’s Call for Experts offers a paid opportunity for researchers, analysts, practitioners and organizations to contribute to the development of practical resources on democratic participation, common values and civic engagement.

Selected contributors will help consolidate research, identify useful tools and networks, annotate key publications and develop accessible content for one or two of six sectors: Higher Education, School Education, Vocational Education and Training, Adult Education, Youth and Sport.

With a fixed fee of €1,250 for one sector or €2,500 for two sectors, the assignment combines professional remuneration with the opportunity to contribute to resources intended for educators, youth workers, sport organizations, programme beneficiaries and other stakeholders.

description: Applications are invited for the 5th International Association for Feminist Economics (IAFFE) Feminist Economics School 2027, an intensive educational programme designed for individuals who want to deepen their understanding of feminist economics, its research methods, and its practical applications in policy, activism, and professional work. The 2027 Feminist Economics School will take place from 29 June to 1 July 2027 at Okayama University in Okayama, Japan. The programme will bring together participants for two and a half days of interactive workshops focused on feminist economic thought, methodologies, and policy applications.

details.overview: Applications are invited for the 5th International Association for Feminist Economics (IAFFE) Feminist Economics School 2027, an intensive educational programme designed for individuals who want to deepen their understanding of feminist economics, its research methods, and its practical applications in policy, activism, and professional work. The 2027 Feminist Economics School will take place from 29 June to 1 July 2027 at Okayama University in Okayama, Japan. The programme will bring together participants for two and a half days of interactive workshops focused on feminist economic thought, methodologies, and policy applications.
whoCanApply: The programme is designed for people who have already engaged with feminist economics questions and issues through professional work, activism, social movements, or advanced academic study.
Applicants should be able to demonstrate both relevant experience and a genuine interest in undertaking deeper study of feminist economics.
The organisers particularly encourage applications from individuals based in the Global South and people from historically discriminated groups around the world.
Applicants may qualify through a minimum of five years of professional work, activism, or social movement experience in areas related to feminist economics.
This route recognises that relevant knowledge and experience may be developed outside formal academic programmes.

For example, an applicant may have worked on issues related to gender and economic inequality, women’s livelihoods, labour conditions, economic justice, unpaid care work, social protection, or other subjects connected to feminist economic questions.
The key requirement is that the experience should be relevant to feminist economics. The application should make the connection between the candidate’s experience and the field clear.
benefits: The form asks several questions about travel funding, disability, accommodation, and travel requirements.

Applicants will need to indicate whether they require full or partial travel funding and provide an estimated amount in US dollars if support is needed. If no travel funding is required, the form instructs applicants to enter “0”.
Candidates must also respond to questions about disability, shared accommodation, and whether a visa is required to travel to Japan.

The form asks whether applicants intend to submit a presentation, paper, or session proposal for the conference and apply for an IAFFE conference travel grant. It also asks whether applicants are IAFFE members and how they learned about the school.
Applicants should answer each question according to their circumstances and follow any instructions shown in the form.
howToApply: Travel grants are available to support selected participants.

These grants may help eligible participants with the costs of travelling to Okayama, Japan. The application form asks candidates to indicate whether they require full or partial travel funding and to estimate the amount required in US dollars.
The announcement does not specify the maximum travel grant, the number of grants available, the selection formula, or whether all requested costs will be covered.
Applicants who require assistance should therefore provide a realistic estimate and explain their needs through the application form.
Applicants must complete the official Feminist Economics School application form.
The organisers state that all sections must be completed and that incomplete submissions will not be considered. After submission, applicants will receive a confirmation email.
The application form collects personal information, educational and employment details, a statement of purpose, and information about funding and other needs.

title: CSW71 SAEF Delegate Application
audience: The application invitation is intended for individuals interested in advancing gender equality and contributing to…
description: The CSW71 SAEF Delegate Application 2027 offers individuals interested in gender equality, women’s empowerment, women’s rights and youth development an opportunity to apply to join the Southern Africa Embrace Foundation (SAEF) delegation to the 71st Session of the United Nations Commission on the Status of Women (CSW71) in New York City, United States. The international gathering will take place from 8 to 19 March 2027, bringing together stakeholders to discuss gender equality and the empowerment of women and girls.

details.overview: The CSW71 SAEF Delegate Application 2027 offers individuals interested in gender equality, women’s empowerment, women’s rights and youth development an opportunity to apply to join the Southern Africa Embrace Foundation (SAEF) delegation to the 71st Session of the United Nations Commission on the Status of Women (CSW71) in New York City, United States. The international gathering will take place from 8 to 19 March 2027, bringing together stakeholders to discuss gender equality and the empowerment of women and girls.
whoCanApply: The application invitation is intended for individuals interested in advancing gender equality and contributing to discussions on women’s empowerment and youth development.

The supplied announcement does not establish a specific nationality, residency, academic qualification or professional experience requirement. Applicants should consult the application form for any additional conditions and should not assume that a particular degree or employment background is mandatory.
The following considerations can help prospective delegates assess whether the opportunity aligns with their interests and circumstances.
Applicants must understand that participation is self-funded.

Selected delegates are responsible for arranging and paying for their own travel, accommodation and related expenses. They must also pay the required CAD $100 donation before official INDIGO registration.
Candidates should assess whether they can meet these financial commitments before applying. The announcement does not promise reimbursement or general travel funding.
Because the event takes place in the United States, international applicants must consider the visa or entry requirements applicable to their circumstances.
benefits: Selected delegates must make the CAD $100 donation before completing official INDIGO registration and receiving the UN ECOSOC approval letter.
Because the contribution is non-refundable, applicants should carefully consider their ability to travel before making the payment.
howToApply: Yes. The announcement expressly states that needing to apply for a visa does not disqualify someone from applying to join the delegation.
Nevertheless, applicants should understand that visa-related circumstances may affect selection priorities and that a visa is not guaranteed.
Interested applicants must complete the online application form before the deadline of 31 December 2026.
The following steps outline the application process and the main considerations applicants should address.

Yes. Applicants who need a visa may still apply. However, SAEF states that priority will be given to applicants who already hold valid US visas, are based in regions with fewer travel restrictions or are from visa-exempt countries.
